label: 1 Peter is addressed to Christians in the province of Pontus

place.note: The address of 1 Peter names the province, not a settlement. Pinned to the Pontus region resource (857287). Pliny (lit-pliny-pontus-bithynia) gives the second, independent attestation for this province a generation later.

date.note: Composition of 1 Peter. Traditional Petrine authorship puts it before Peter's death under Nero (c. 64); the majority view holds it pseudonymous, c. 70–90. Harnack (p. 186 n.) assigns it to 'the earlier years of Domitian' (c. 81–85). Upper bound 96 (end of Domitian); a minority dates it into the early second century.

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 92–93 (register of communities traceable before Trajan), 186

notes: 1 Peter 1.1 addresses 'the elect exiles of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia' — five provinces, entered here as five region-level items. Harnack's register lists 'a number of churches in Bithynia and Pontus (1 Pet. i. 1; Pliny's ep. to Trajan).'
